text_blocks.snippet: Type 1 diabetes in children is diagnosed through blood tests that measure blood sugar levels and an A1C test, which reflects average blood sugar over time. A random blood sugar level of 200 mg/dL or higher, or a fasting blood sugar level of 126 mg/dL or higher, along with symptoms, can indicate diabetes. An A1C level of 6.5% or higher on two separate tests is also a diagnostic indicator.
snippet_highlighted_words: blood tests that measure blood sugar levels and an A1C test

list.title: 1. Initial Assessment:
list.snippet: Doctors will typically start with a physical exam and inquire about the child's symptoms.
Random Blood Sugar Test: A blood sample is taken at any time, and a level of 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or higher, along with symptoms, suggests diabetes.
Fasting Blood Sugar Test: A blood sample is taken after an overnight fast (at least 8 hours), and a level of 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or higher indicates diabetes.
Oral Glucose Tolerance Test (OGTT): Involves drinking a sugary solution and having blood sugar levels checked periodically for up to 2 hours, according to the Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

list.title: 3. A1C Test:
list.snippet: Measures the average blood sugar level over the past 2-3 months. An A1C level of 6.5% or higher suggests diabetes.
Extreme hunger and unexplained weight loss
Frequent diaper changes in infants or bedwetting in older children
Fruity-smelling breath, nausea, vomiting, or stomach pain (especially in cases of diabetic ketoacidosis)

text_blocks.snippet: Important Note: Early diagnosis and treatment of type 1 diabetes are crucial to prevent serious complications. If you suspect your child may have diabetes, seek prompt medical attention.
